AttachmentRef.description:
Ride on a point of another entity instead of standing on your own.

This is how a separately-generated weapon ends up in a separately-
generated character's hand. Tripo sometimes returns "goblin holding a
rifle" as one mesh and sometimes returns two, and only the second case
needs this -- but it is common enough that a scene with no way to express
it cannot build half the games it is asked for.

anchor.description: Socket or rig joint on the parent to follow. Named sockets ('muzzle', 'grip') win; otherwise the runtime matches a joint, including loose aliases like 'hand_r' / 'hand_l' / 'head' that work regardless of what Tripo named the bones.
anchor.title: Anchor

entity_id.description: The entity to ride on, by scene entity id.
entity_id.title: Entity Id

position.description: Offset from the anchor, in the anchor's space (metres).

socket.description: Optional socket on THIS entity (e.g. 'grip') to seat on the anchor, so a rifle sits in an NPC's hand by its own handle. Overrides position/rotation.
socket.title: Socket

AttachmentRef.title: AttachmentRef

attached_to.description: Parent this entity to a point on another one. Its transform is then driven by the parent every frame, so the authored 'transform' above is only its pose before the first update.

equip_slots.description: Places items can be equipped ON THIS ENTITY. Declare these on the WEARER (the player rig or an NPC), not on the holster, sheath or rack prop. Required for 'builtin.equip' to have anywhere to put anything.
equip_slots.title: Equip Slots

faction.description: Which side this entity is on. Required for anything that selects targets or can be targeted.

health.description: Give this entity hit points. Required for anything that can be killed or can take damage.

placement.description: Where it belongs relative to the world. Required for anything that rests on furniture, hangs, mounts on a wall or stands at a world feature.

satisfies.description: Ids of the requirements (requirements.json) this entity's existence and placement satisfy.
satisfies.title: Satisfies

EquipSlotSpec.description:
One place something can be equipped ON THIS ENTITY.

Mirrors the runtime ``ptv::EquipSlot`` field for field. The distinction
that matters: a mesh SOCKET is a point on an item ("the muzzle of this
rifle"), while an equip SLOT is a place on a WEARER that an item can go
("the holster on this player's right hip"). Holstering is therefore
declared on the player or the NPC, never on the holster prop.

``builtin.equip`` reads these to decide where a released item can snap,
and its ``params.slots`` filters by ``name``. A wearer with no declared
slots offers no candidates, so an equip binding on such an entity can
never fire -- which is why the scene compiler fails the build for it.

accepts_tags.description: Item tags this slot accepts, matched against the item entity's 'tags'. Empty accepts anything, which is how a sword ends up holstered just because it brushed the player's hip.
accepts_tags.title: Accepts Tags

body_slot.description: Canonical body slot this sits on: 'hand_r', 'hand_l', 'waist', 'wrist_l', 'wrist_r', 'chest', 'back', 'head'. Leave empty ONLY when the slot is hosted by another equipped item.
body_slot.title: Body Slot

exclusive.description: One item at a time; equipping replaces the incumbent.
exclusive.title: Exclusive

host_item_slot.description: Name of the slot whose equipped ITEM hosts this slot, for gear that mounts on other gear (a mask hose on a back tank). Empty for an ordinary body slot.
host_item_slot.title: Host Item Slot

host_socket.description: Socket on the hosting item. Empty for a body slot.
host_socket.title: Host Socket

local_position.description: Offset from the body slot or host socket, in metres.

name.description: Slot name gameplay refers to, e.g. 'hand_r', 'hip_holster_r', 'sword_sheath_l'. Must be unique on this entity.
name.title: Name

snap_radius_m.description: How close a released item must be to snap in. 0 means proximity is not required (menu- or script-driven equipping). Use 0.15-0.25 for a hip holster the player reaches for.
snap_radius_m.title: Snap Radius M

EquipSlotSpec.title: EquipSlotSpec

FactionProps.description:
Which side an entity fights for.

Needed so enemies engage the player's allied NPCs and not only the
player. Use short stable ids: 'player', 'enemy', 'ally', 'wildlife'.
FactionProps.title: FactionProps

HealthProps.description: Hit points for anything that can be damaged, including the player.

invuln_after_hit_s.description: Invulnerability window after each hit. Contact damage is tested every frame, so without one a single touch empties a health bar in a few frames.
invuln_after_hit_s.title: Invuln After Hit S

HealthProps.title: HealthProps

HoldRef.description:
How a held item is solved into the hand(s); compiled from the
InteractionDesign + asset contract. The SceneSpec agent leaves it empty.
HoldRef.title: HoldRef

mechanic_id.description: Either 'builtin.<name>' for a reusable mechanic or 'generated.<code_task_id>' for a generated module.
mechanic_id.title: Mechanic Id

hold.description: Hold profile for held items, compiled by the scene compiler from interaction_design.json. The SceneSpec agent leaves this empty.

sockets.description: Named attachment points (e.g. 'muzzle', 'grip') in metres, relative to the mesh origin. Populated by the scene compiler from asset_contract.json; the SceneSpec agent leaves this empty.
sockets.title: Sockets

PlacementRelation.description: How an entity relates to the world it sits in.
PlacementRelation.title: PlacementRelation

PlacementSpec.description:
WHERE an entity belongs, in terms of the world -- not coordinates.

The scene composer writes this; the world architect builds the furniture
and declares an anchor (or an anchor SET, for runtime spawns) for every
request; the scene compiler rests the entity on it using the mesh's
measured bounds. Coordinates in ``transform`` are then only a fallback.

anchor.description: Id of the world anchor this entity uses, e.g. 'firearms_table_glock'. The world must declare it.
anchor.title: Anchor

anchor_set.description: For a TEMPLATE spawned at runtime: id of the world anchor set whose points it is spawned at, e.g. 'lane2_hang_points'.
anchor_set.title: Anchor Set

count.description: How many points the anchor_set needs.
count.title: Count

description.description: Where it goes in plain words: 'on the left end of the firearms table', 'hanging under the red poles in lane 2'.
description.title: Description

PlacementSpec.title: PlacementSpec

QuatXYZW.description: Quaternion stored as (x, y, z, w), identity = (0,0,0,1).
QuatXYZW.title: QuatXYZW

SocketRef.description:
A named attachment point in the mesh's own local space.

Derived deterministically from geometry by the ``asset_contract`` stage
and converted from unit space to metres by the scene compiler, so the
runtime can just compose ``entity_transform * socket``.

kind.description: Socket kind (hand_grip, muzzle, ...). Hand kinds are in the OpenXR grip frame; every other kind faces along +Z.
kind.title: Kind

SocketRef.title: SocketRef
